cells.tense: You are here at the present moment, and both the clear sight and the timing are in your hands.
cells.ask: Offer one correction to the group lightly, then leave it standing where you put it.
cells.core:
You're holding what's clear in front of people, and you know when to say it. Not blunt, not silent — it goes out once, in words that land, and then you let it stand. The timing is the whole thing, and it's working right now. Somebody in the room says the true thing at the right moment and a shared thing stays alive because of it.

It bends when you reach back in to check it landed, or say it a second time. Say it once and leave the room to do what it does with it. Nothing here needs you standing by the door waiting to hear how it went. Keeping that timing clean is what holding this costs.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's clear and you say it at the right time.
cells.verb: seeing a thing clearly and picking the moment it gets said
cells.place: in what a group carries forward and keeps meaning together

cells.tense: You are correcting what has not been said yet, bracing for a moment still ahead of this one.
cells.ask: Let one wrong thing in the group stand for a day without touching it.
cells.core:
The clarity is running ahead of the room. Somewhere forward there's a version where the shared thing has already been said right, and you're living there — so a talk with people becomes a chance to sharpen it before it's ripe, to get in first. The correcting is spending something the correcting was meant to protect.

It bends when the moment you're answering hasn't arrived. Say the thing once, then keep your hands off it. A group's meaning settles on its own when someone trusts it enough not to reach in. What this costs to keep is the patience of not knowing yet whether it landed.

cells.tense: You had hold of this once, and you are still at a threshold the day has already passed.
cells.ask: Say one plain thing about what feels true in a group you already sit in, once, out loud.
cells.core:
The clear read is there and it isn't going out. You know what you think and the sentence doesn't get said. Meanwhile the shared thing around you moves without your hand on it. Well-held, this looks like one true sentence offered to a room you already belong to, said without armor, received however it lands.

It bends toward staying quiet — the offering has stopped while the understanding hasn't. Start smaller than feels worth it. One plain sentence to one person in a group you already sit in, today or this week. Nothing needs to come back from it. You don't need the reply to make the sentence worth saying.
cells.sheetLine: You have something clear to say and you've gone quiet.

cells.tense: You are already setting what the group treats as sayable, and you describe that as just being careful.
cells.ask: Name one thing about how you talk in the group as a choice you made.
cells.core:
The shaping is running. The words you pick, the tone you set, the things you let pass — those are already deciding what counts as true in the room. But the shaping gets filed under the group, or under being careful, or under the way things are. At its cleanest, this looks like one true sentence offered to a room you belong to, timing and all, and it's yours.

It bends when the pen is moving and the hand isn't on it. Take one piece back: a phrase you use, a standard you keep, a thing you won't say. Naming it once doesn't make you big — it makes the shaping usable, by you and by the room.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping this. You just haven't owned it.
